chunks: With this chain of narrators, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, from Yahya ibn Sabur, that he said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the dead person shedding a tear at the moment of death. He said: That is when he is to be observed by the Messenger of Allah (Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family), during which he will see that which makes him rejoice and which he loves. He said: Then he said: Do you not see a man, he sees what rejoices him and what he loves, during which his eye will shed a tear and he will smile?

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Why does a dying person's eye shed a tear or smile according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq narrates this hadith to illustrate the concept of *mawt al-saghir* (minor death), where the dying person witnesses the reality of the Hereafter through the presence of the Prophet. This immediate visual confirmation of their spiritual state—whether joy or sorrow—serves as a tangible sign of their inner readiness to meet Allah, reinforcing the Shia belief in the continuity of consciousness and perception after the soul's separation from the body.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	With this chain of narrators, from Ali bin Mahziyar, from Fadala bin Ayub, from Mu’awiya bin Wahab, from Yahya bin Sabour, that he said:

I heard Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, speaking with regards to the dead person when his eye sheds a tear at (the moment of) death. He said: That is when he is to be observed by the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, during which he will see that which makes him rejoice and which he loves. He said: Then he said: Do you not see a man, he sees what rejoices him and what he loves, during which his eye will shed a tear and he will smile?
